title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - NovaWorks
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked NovaWorks through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdown. Discussed routing policies, caching, dedicated vs hosted, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Customer requested pricing details, SOC2 artifact, and a short POC to run production-like traffic for cost validation.
topics: Caching / KV cache and batching tradeoffs
next_steps: Jamie to send detailed pricing + SKU sheet by 2026-03-03
Marcus to share security pack (SOC2 summary + KMS notes) by 2026-03-04
Schedule a 2-week POC load test with NovaWorks test dataset (target week of 2026-03-15)
Follow-up demo for Dedicated capacity scenarios week of 2026-03-08
action_items: Jamie Chen: Send pricing and SKU sheet (due 2026-03-03)
Marcus Patel: Share SOC2 excerpt and KMS integration notes (due 2026-03-04)
Carlos Mendez: Provide sample workload profile and peak QPS numbers (due 2026-03-02)
Sophie Nguyen: Confirm stakeholders and legal contacts for pilot (due 2026-03-05)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Linda Park (NovaWorks CTO), Carlos Mendez (NovaWorks MLOps), Sophie Nguyen (NovaWorks Eng Lead)

[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jamie chen, i'm the AE on this account. quick check, everyone can hear me?
[00:10] Linda (NovaWorks): yes loud and clear, thanks jamie.
[00:27] Jamie: cool. today Marcus and i will do a quick console walk through — focus on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the token-level cost breakdown since i know you asked about unit economics.
[00:40] Marcus (Redwood SE): hi all, i'll jump in on the dashboard live demo, show how to filter by route, by model, and how the cost breakdown maps to tokens and inference time. some of the labels on your screen might look a bit off, we had a small display quirk in staging earlier.
[01:10] Carlos (NovaWorks): quick question before you dive in — we run multi-tenant microservices that hit models with varying sequence lengths, will we be able to see per-route seq len distribution?
[01:22] Marcus: yes, under the route details there's a sequence length distribution and percentile latencies. it also shows kernel selection hints — so you can see when a quantized variant was used vs full fp16.
[01:40] Jamie: i'll pull up the Routes page now — you can see average tokens per request, cost per route, p50/p95 latency and a sparkline for errors.
[01:55] [screen share sound] Marcus: so here's the per-route dashboard, top-left is total tokens consumed last 30 days, you can drop down to 24 hours. filters on the right let you slice by model family, region, and plan.
[02:20] Sophie (NovaWorks): are you aggregating cache hits? we use a lot of prefix caching for chat history.
[02:30] Marcus: yes, cache hit rate is shown and you can drill into KV cache effectiveness with hit/miss ratios and request examples. note: cache labels sometimes show as KV-cache in the UI but we also support prefix-level caching.
[02:50] Linda: on cost, does the console show per-token charge vs infra cost? like how much our bill vs actual GPU hours?
[03:03] Marcus: good question. there's two views — bill view and unit economics view. the unit view breaks down token cost, effective GPU time, batching efficiency and amortized kernel cost. it can export CSV for your finops team.
[03:20] Jamie: i'll jump to the Cost Breakdown report — this maps route -> model variant -> token count -> token cost. we also surface model fallbacks if a cheaper variant was used during bursts.
[03:45] [background typing noise] Carlos: sometimes model names in your export come back garbled, we saw that in the last export, any chance of that?
[03:54] Marcus: yep we've seen minor transcription style issues in model identifiers when aliases are long — we'll include a cleaned export script in the POC materials.
[04:10] Sophie: latency histograms — can we create alerts on p95 crossing thresholds? and tie that to routing policies?
[04:22] Marcus: yep, alerts can be created per-route and can trigger automatic routing policy changes — example: move traffic to a lower-latency region or fallback to a compatible model variant. the policy is in the Rollouts tab.
[04:40] Jamie: wanted to call out the Live Trace view — you can select a problematic request and see token-by-token timing and where KV cache reads happened. super helpful for debugging tail latency.
[05:05] Linda: security — we need SOC2 and KMS details. we also have a strict VPC-only requirement for the pilot.
[05:14] Jamie: understood. we support Private (VPC) deployments and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. we'll share the SOC2 attestation and the architecture note.
[05:30] Marcus: adding to that, audit logs are in the Console under Security -> Audit and exportable for your SIEM. RBAC roles let you restrict route creation and model rollouts.
[05:48] Carlos: for a pilot, we'd like to run production-like traffic — around 200 concurrent users and peaks at 120 QPS for inference. is that feasible?
[05:58] Marcus: yes, we can replicate that in our Dedicated staging; batching and autoscale policies will matter. i'll propose a config for dedicated GPU pools and burst policy.
[06:15] Jamie: regarding pricing — we have hosted per-token pricing, and reserved pricing for Dedicated with commit tiers. i'll follow up with a pricing sheet, should include sample scenarios based on your QPS.
[06:30] [pause] Carlos: on observability, can we correlate costs with feature flags or product routes? we want to know which product feature is driving the bill.
[06:42] Marcus: you can tag routes with metadata (product/team/feature). the analytics view will group by tags so you can attribute cost to product features.
[07:00] Sophie: do you support model quantization recommendations? we've been evaluating 4-bit for some cost wins but worried about regression.
[07:10] Marcus: yes — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per model based on your evals, and the Console will show quality regressions tied to prompt sets. we also support automatic fallback to higher-precision model variants when regressions are detected.
[07:35] Linda: legal will want exportable docs and an audit trail, also proof of where data is stored for residency requirements.
[07:45] Jamie: noted, we'll include a data residency map and the audit log export instructions.
[08:00] [several minutes of demo navigation, showing charts and CSV export]
[15:10] Marcus: jumping ahead to the Token Timeline — this visualizes tokens over time and overlays cost per token by model variant. here you can see a spike where a fallback happened and cost doubled for that window.
[15:35] Carlos: would the fallback always increase cost? could it sometimes reduce cost if it routed to a cheaper model?
[15:45] Marcus: yes both possible. fallback policies can be configured by cost or latency preference. for example, during congestion you might fallback to a cheaper quantized variant to keep throughput up.
[16:05] Jamie: quick note on billing reconciliation — the Console export has a detailed ledger that ties tokens to charge lines; many customers ingest that into their internal chargeback system.
[16:25] Sophie: any limitations on CSV exports? we have automated ingestion, so want consistent schema.
[16:32] Marcus: schema is stable but column names may evolve; we'll provide a versioned export and a mapping file in the POC repo.
[16:50] Linda: if we go Dedicated, what's the SLA?
[16:58] Jamie: Dedicated has an SLA for throughput and latency tiers depending on commit level. the exact numbers live in the SLO addendum, which i'll share. for VPC/private deployments there's an enterprise SLA negotiated in the contract.
[17:15] Carlos: curious about real-world efficiency gains — do you have metrics for batching improvements?
[17:22] Marcus: yes — in the Optimize section we show batching efficiency and expected token-per-GPU improvements. we can run a simulation on your workload to estimate 20-40% token cost reduction depending on prompt lengths and burstiness.
[17:45] Sophie: what's the typical uplift/loss when using 4-bit quant vs fp16 for our class of models?
[17:52] Marcus: usually 10-25% inference speedup, but quality impact depends on use-case — Optimize will run evals on your prompt sets and give a confidence score.
[18:10] [brief cross-talk] Speaker 1: uh and also like i saw earlier the dashboard said kernel selection 'nv-kernel-72' — what's that?
[18:18] Marcus: that's the compiled kernel name, primarily internal, but we surface it so engineers can correlate performance differences across infra generations.
[18:40] Linda: can you show a route-level example where caching saved us money?
[18:48] Marcus: sure — here's a customer example: route 'convo-history' had a 65% cache hit and cost per 1k tokens was 35% lower. you can export the sample requests that hit/miss the cache for debug.
[19:10] Carlos: for the pilot, we'll need a clean export and mapping to our product features. we'll also want a forensic log for a few requests.
[19:20] Jamie: we'll supply sample exports and a small tool to reconcile route ids to product features.
[19:30] [lag, slight audio glitch]
[20:05] Marcus: switching to Rollouts — here's how you set up canary and A/B traffic splits, and create automatic fallback policies on error/latency thresholds.
[20:30] Sophie: in canaries, can we limit by user group? we only want to target internal testers.
[20:36] Marcus: yes, you can target by tags or add a header-based rule to route only requests with a given test flag.
[21:00] Linda: SOC2 and encryption — will customer-managed KMS mean logs are still accessible to Redwood ops?
[21:10] Jamie: with customer-managed KMS the data at rest is encrypted under your key; audit logs for the control plane are available to Redwood but content-level access can be restricted. we'll send the exact matrix.
[21:35] Carlos: do you have integrations to our SIEM? we use Splunk.
[21:42] Marcus: yes audit log export can push to S3 and you can wire S3 to Splunk; we'll provide an architecture note.
[22:00] Sophie: i want to see the Deployment Config you recommended for our 120 QPS peak.
[22:10] Marcus: i'll propose: a dedicated pool with 4 GPUs, autoscale to 8 for bursts, batch size target 32, and KV cache enabled with 10k prefix entries. i'll attach config to the POC repo.
[22:35] Jamie: pricing example — for hosted at your volume, you see per-token cost X, while Dedicated with reserved commits plus autoscale amortization gives you Y% lower per-token but requires 3-month commit. i'll send scenarios.
[23:00] Linda: can we have a pilot without commit? we prefer short evaluation first.
[23:07] Jamie: yes, short POC on Hosted or Dedicated staging works; committed pricing only if you go long-term.
[23:25] [demo continues, showing Optimize recommendations and quality monitoring]
[30:40] Marcus: in the Quality Monitoring view you can pin prompt sets and see quality regressions; alerts can be created if generations drop below a threshold. this ties into rollbacks.
[31:05] Carlos: do rollbacks automatically move traffic to older model versions?
[31:12] Marcus: yes we support automatic or manual rollbacks; you can pin a stable model version as a baseline.
[31:30] Sophie: how long does it take to onboard a new model to the Console for analytics?
[31:36] Marcus: pretty quick — once the model is deployed it appears in the catalog and traffic starts flowing in; analytics populate within minutes but full historical metrics need a few hours.
[31:55] Linda: anything else we should plan for on our side?
[32:02] Carlos: we'll provide sample logs, traffic profile, and a scoping doc for the pilot.
[32:10] Jamie: perfect. next steps recap. i'll send pricing and the SLO addendum, Marcus will send the security pack and the proposed Dedicated config, and we'll set up the POC for week of 2026-03-15.
[32:35] Sophie: can we get a follow-up dedicated deep dive on batching sometime next week?
[32:43] Marcus: yes i'll schedule a batching deep dive — propose 60 minutes, bring infra and model engineers.
[33:00] [wrap up small talk]
[33:20] Jamie: thanks everyone, i'll email the notes and action items.
[33:28] Linda: thanks, bye.
[33:31] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution inaccuracies (Speaker 1), minor transcription errors on kernel names and long model aliases. CSV exports and artifact links to be provided in follow-up email.
